sanskrit: tasya tac chidram ājñāya dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ samutthitaḥ khaḍgī rathād avaplutya sahasā droṇam abhyayāt
english: Marking that opening of his, Dhṛṣṭadyumna rose up, sword in hand, and leaping suddenly down from his chariot rushed upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtāni bhūtāni mānuṣāṇītarāṇi ca droṇaṃ tathāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭadyumnavaśaṃ gatam
english: All beings, men and others alike, cried out in horror to see Droṇa brought to such a pass, fallen into Dhṛṣṭadyumna's power.

sanskrit: hāhākāraṃ bhṛśaṃ cakrur aho dhig iti cābruvan droṇo 'pi śastrāṇy utsṛjya paramaṃ sāmyam āsthitaḥ
english: They raised a great wail and cried, "Alas! Shame!" And Droṇa himself, casting aside his weapons, took his stand in the highest equanimity.

sanskrit: tathoktvā yogam āsthāya jyotirbhūto mahātapāḥ divam ākrāmad ācāryaḥ sadbhiḥ saha durākramam
english: Having so spoken, the great ascetic took to yoga and, become pure light, the teacher ascended to that heaven hard to attain, together with the holy ones.

sanskrit: dvau sūryāv iti no buddhir āsīt tasmiṃs tathā gate ekāgram iva cāsīd dhi jyotirbhiḥ pūritaṃ nabhaḥ samapadyata cārkābhe bhāradvājaniśākare
english: When he passed on in that manner, our thought was that there were two suns; the sky, filled with radiances, seemed gathered into one, and the son of Bharadvāja, like the moon, took on the splendor of the sun.

sanskrit: nimeṣamātreṇa ca taj jyotir antaradhīyata āsīt kilakilāśabdaḥ prahṛṣṭānāṃ divaukasām brahmalokaṃ gate droṇe dhṛṣṭadyumne ca mohite
english: In the space of an eye's blink that light vanished away; there arose a glad clamor of the rejoicing dwellers of heaven, now that Droṇa had gone to the world of Brahmā and Dhṛṣṭadyumna stood bewildered.

sanskrit: vayam eva tadādrākṣma pañca mānuṣayonayaḥ yogayuktaṃ mahātmānaṃ gacchantaṃ paramāṃ gatim
english: We five alone, born of human wombs, beheld the great-souled one, yoked in yoga, going to the supreme goal.

sanskrit: ahaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ pārthaḥ kṛpaḥ śāradvato dvijaḥ vāsudevaś ca vārṣṇeyo dharmarājaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: I, and Dhanaṃjaya the son of Pṛthā, and Kṛpa the brahmin son of Śaradvat, and Vāsudeva of the Vṛṣṇis, and the Pāṇḍava Yudhiṣṭhira the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: anye tu sarve nāpaśyan bhāradvājasya dhīmataḥ mahimānaṃ mahārāja yogamuktasya gacchataḥ
english: But all the others did not see, O great king, the glory of the wise son of Bharadvāja as, freed by yoga, he departed.

sanskrit: gatiṃ paramikāṃ prāptam ajānanto nṛyonayaḥ nāpaśyan gacchamānaṃ hi taṃ sārdham ṛṣipuṃgavaiḥ ācāryaṃ yogam āsthāya brahmalokam ariṃdamam
english: Not knowing that he had attained the supreme goal, the human-born ones did not see the teacher going, together with the bulls among sages, taking to yoga toward the world of Brahmā—he, the tamer of foes.

sanskrit: vitunnāṅgaṃ śaraśatair nyastāyudham asṛkkṣaram dhikkṛtaḥ pārṣatas taṃ tu sarvabhūtaiḥ parāmṛśat
english: His limbs pierced by hundreds of arrows, his weapons laid down, streaming with blood—him the son of Pṛṣata seized, though reproached for it by all beings.

sanskrit: tasya mūrdhānam ālambya gatasattvasya dehinaḥ kiṃ cid abruvataḥ kāyād vicakartāsinā śiraḥ
english: Grasping the head of that embodied one whose life had fled and who spoke not a word, he severed the head from the body with his sword.

sanskrit: harṣeṇa mahatā yukto bhāradvāje nipātite siṃhanādaravaṃ cakre bhrāmayan khaḍgam āhave
english: Filled with mighty joy now that the son of Bharadvāja had been struck down, he raised a lion's roar, brandishing his sword upon the field.

sanskrit: ākarṇapalitaḥ śyāmo vayasāśītipañcakaḥ tvatkṛte vyacarat saṃkhye sa tu ṣoḍaśavarṣavat
english: Gray-haired to the ears, dark of hue, eighty-five years of age, yet for your sake he had ranged the battle like one of sixteen years.

sanskrit: uktavāṃś ca mahābāhuḥ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ jīvantam ānayācāryaṃ mā vadhīr drupadātmaja
english: And the mighty-armed Dhanaṃjaya, son of Kuntī, had cried out, "Bring the teacher to me alive! Do not slay him, O son of Drupada!"

sanskrit: na hantavyo na hantavya iti te sainikāś ca ha utkrośann arjunaś caiva sānukrośas tam ādravat
english: "He must not be slain, he must not be slain!"—so cried the soldiers too, and Arjuna himself, full of compassion, ran toward him.

sanskrit: krośamāne 'rjune caiva pārthiveṣu ca sarvaśaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumno 'vadhīd droṇaṃ rathatalpe nararṣabham
english: Yet though Arjuna cried out, and all the kings on every side, Dhṛṣṭadyumna slew Droṇa, that bull among men, upon the floor of his chariot.

sanskrit: śoṇitena pariklinno rathād bhūmim ariṃdamaḥ lohitāṅga ivādityo durdarśaḥ samapadyata evaṃ taṃ nihataṃ saṃkhye dadṛśe sainiko janaḥ
english: Drenched in blood, that tamer of foes, fallen from chariot to ground, became hard to look upon, like the sun with the body of Mars; and so the host of soldiers beheld him slain in battle.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu tad rājan bhāradvājaśiro mahat tāvakānāṃ maheṣvāsaḥ pramukhe tat samākṣipat
english: Then Dhṛṣṭadyumna, that great archer, O king, hurled the great head of Bharadvāja's son before the very faces of your men.

sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭvā śiro rājan bhāradvājasya tāvakāḥ palāyanakṛtotsāhā dudruvuḥ sarvatodiśam
english: And when your men, O king, beheld the head of Bharadvāja's son, their whole resolve turned to flight, and they fled in every direction.

sanskrit: droṇas tu divam āsthāya nakṣatrapatham āviśat aham eva tadādrākṣaṃ droṇasya nidhanaṃ nṛpa
english: But Droṇa, taking to the sky, entered the pathway of the stars; I alone, O king, beheld the passing of Droṇa.

sanskrit: ṛṣeḥ prasādāt kṛṣṇasya satyavatyāḥ sutasya ca vidhūmām iva saṃyāntīm ulkāṃ prajvalitām iva apaśyāma divaṃ stabdhvā gacchantaṃ taṃ mahādyutim
english: By the grace of the seer Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, the son of Satyavatī, we beheld him of great splendor mounting and traversing the sky, like a blazing meteor coursing on, smokeless and aflame.

sanskrit: hate droṇe nirutsāhān kurūn pāṇḍavasṛñjayāḥ abhyadravan mahāvegās tataḥ sainyaṃ vyadīryata
english: When Droṇa was slain, the Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas charged with great fury upon the dispirited Kurus, and thereupon the army was torn asunder.

sanskrit: nihatā hayabhūyiṣṭhāḥ saṃgrāme niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ tāvakā nihate droṇe gatāsava ivābhavan
english: Most of them slain along with their horses in battle by whetted arrows, your men, with Droṇa slain, became as if their breath had fled.

sanskrit: parājayam athāvāpya paratra ca mahad bhayam ubhayenaiva te hīnā nāvindan dhṛtim ātmanaḥ
english: Having met with defeat, and with great dread of the world beyond, undone by both alike, they could find no steadiness in themselves.

sanskrit: anvicchantaḥ śarīraṃ tu bhāradvājasya pārthivāḥ nādhyagacchaṃs tadā rājan kabandhāyutasaṃkule
english: The kings, searching for the body of Bharadvāja's son, could not then find it, O king, in that press thronged with ten thousand headless trunks.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu jayaṃ labdhvā paratra ca mahad yaśaḥ bāṇaśabdaravāṃś cakruḥ siṃhanādāṃś ca puṣkalān
english: But the Pāṇḍavas, having won the victory and great fame in the world beyond, made the twang of bowstrings ring out and raised abundant lion-roars.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tato rājan dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ varūthinyām anṛtyetāṃ pariṣvajya parasparam
english: Then, O king, Bhīmasena and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata danced amid the host, embracing one another.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā bhīmaḥ pārṣataṃ śatrutāpanam bhūyo 'haṃ tvāṃ vijayinaṃ pariṣvakṣyāmi pārṣata sūtaputre hate pāpe dhārtarāṣṭre ca saṃyuge
english: And Bhīma then said to the son of Pṛṣata, the scorcher of foes, "Again I shall embrace you victorious, O son of Pṛṣata, when the wicked son of the charioteer and the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra are slain in battle."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā bhīmas tu harṣeṇa mahatā yutaḥ bāhuśabdena pṛthivīṃ kampayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Having said only this much, Bhīma the Pāṇḍava, filled with mighty joy, made the earth quake with the clapping of his arms.

sanskrit: tasya śabdena vitrastāḥ prādravaṃs tāvakā yudhi kṣatradharmaṃ samutsṛjya palāyanaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Terrified by that sound, your men fled in the battle, casting aside the warrior's code and bent wholly upon flight.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu jayaṃ labdhvā hṛṣṭā hy āsan viśāṃ pate arikṣayaṃ ca saṃgrāme tena te sukham āpnuvan
english: But the Pāṇḍavas, having won the victory, were glad, O lord of peoples, and through the destruction of their foes in battle they attained happiness.

sanskrit: tato droṇe hate rājan kuravaḥ śastrapīḍitāḥ hatapravīrā vidhvastā bhṛśaṃ śokaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Then, O king, with Droṇa slain, the Kurus, sorely afflicted by weapons, their champions struck down, shattered, were given over utterly to grief.

sanskrit: vicetaso hatotsāhāḥ kaśmalābhihataujasaḥ ārtasvareṇa mahatā putraṃ te paryavārayan
english: Bereft of sense, their courage broken, their vigor smitten with faintness, with a great cry of anguish they thronged about your son.

sanskrit: rajasvalā vepamānā vīkṣamāṇā diśo daśa aśrukaṇṭhā yathā daityā hiraṇyākṣe purā hate
english: Covered with dust, trembling, gazing about the ten directions, their throats choked with tears, like the Daityas of old when Hiraṇyākṣa was slain.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛto rājā trastaiḥ kṣudramṛgair iva aśaknuvann avasthātum apāyāt tanayas tava
english: Surrounded by them, terrified as they were like little beasts, your son the king, unable to hold his ground, withdrew.

sanskrit: kṣutpipāsāpariśrāntās te yodhās tava bhārata ādityena ca saṃtaptā bhṛśaṃ vimanaso 'bhavan
english: Worn out by hunger and thirst, those warriors of yours, O Bhārata, and scorched by the sun, became utterly disheartened.

sanskrit: bhāskarasyeva patanaṃ samudrasyeva śoṣaṇam viparyāsaṃ yathā meror vāsavasyeva nirjayam
english: It was as though the sun had fallen, as though the ocean had dried up, as though Meru had been overturned, as though Vāsava himself had been vanquished.

sanskrit: amarṣaṇīyaṃ tad dṛṣṭvā bhāradvājasya pātanam trastarūpatarā rājan kauravāḥ prādravan bhayāt
english: Beholding that unbearable downfall of Bharadvāja's son, the Kauravas, O king, more terror-stricken still, fled in fear.

sanskrit: gāndhārarājaḥ śakunis trastas trastataraiḥ saha hataṃ rukmarathaṃ dṛṣṭvā prādravat sahito rathaiḥ
english: Śakuni, king of the Gāndhāras, terrified, together with those more terrified still, seeing the lord of the golden chariot slain, fled away with his chariots.

sanskrit: varūthinīṃ vegavatīṃ vidrutāṃ sapatākinīm parigṛhya mahāsenāṃ sūtaputro 'payād bhayāt
english: Gathering up the swift army in its rout, with its banners, that great host, the son of the charioteer withdrew in fear.

sanskrit: rathanāgāśvakalilāṃ puraskṛtya tu vāhinīm madrāṇām īśvaraḥ śalyo vīkṣamāṇo 'payād bhayāt
english: Setting before him the army thronged with chariots, elephants, and horses, Śalya, lord of the Madras, gazing about, withdrew in fear.

sanskrit: hatapravīrair bhūyiṣṭhaṃ dvipair bahupadātibhiḥ vṛtaḥ śāradvato 'gacchat kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭam iti bruvan
english: Surrounded by elephants whose champions were mostly slain and by many footmen, the son of Śaradvat went off crying, "Woe, woe!"

sanskrit: bhojānīkena śiṣṭena kaliṅgāraṭṭabāhlikaiḥ kṛtavarmā vṛto rājan prāyāt sujavanair hayaiḥ
english: Surrounded by the remnant of the Bhoja host and by the Kaliṅgas, Āraṭṭas, and Bāhlīkas, Kṛtavarman, O king, went forth on his swift horses.

sanskrit: padātigaṇasaṃyuktas trasto rājan bhayārditaḥ ulūkaḥ prādravat tatra dṛṣṭvā droṇaṃ nipātitam
english: Joined with a band of footmen, terrified and stricken with fear, Ulūka there fled away, O king, on seeing Droṇa struck down.

sanskrit: darśanīyo yuvā caiva śaurye ca kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ duḥśāsano bhṛśodvignaḥ prādravad gajasaṃvṛtaḥ
english: Comely and young, and marked out for his valor, Duḥśāsana, deeply agitated, fled away surrounded by his elephants.

sanskrit: gajāśvarathasaṃyukto vṛtaś caiva padātibhiḥ duryodhano mahārāja prāyāt tatra mahārathaḥ
english: Joined with elephants, horses, and chariots, and surrounded by footmen, Duryodhana, O great king, that mighty chariot-warrior, went off from there.

sanskrit: gajān rathān samāruhya parasyāpi hayāñ janāḥ prakīrṇakeśā vidhvastā na dvāv ekatra dhāvataḥ
english: Mounting elephants, chariots, and even the horses of another, the men with hair flying loose, shattered, ran—no two together in one place.

sanskrit: nedam astīti puruṣā hatotsāhā hataujasaḥ utsṛjya kavacān anye prādravaṃs tāvakā vibho
english: "This is the end!"—so cried the men, their courage broken, their vigor gone; and others of your folk, casting off their armor, fled away, O lord.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ te samākrośan sainikā bharatarṣabha tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti na ca te svayaṃ tatrāvatasthire
english: The soldiers called out to one another, O bull of the Bhāratas, "Stand! Stand!"—yet they themselves did not stand their ground there.

sanskrit: dhuryān pramucya tu rathād dhatasūtān svalaṃkṛtān adhiruhya hayān yodhāḥ kṣipraṃ padbhir acodayan
english: Loosing the well-adorned draught-horses from chariots whose drivers were slain, the warriors mounted them and urged them swiftly on with their heels.

sanskrit: dravamāṇe tathā sainye trastarūpe hataujasi pratisrota iva grāho droṇaputraḥ parān iyāt
english: As the army thus fled, terror-stricken and stripped of vigor, the son of Droṇa moved against the foe like a crocodile breasting the current.

sanskrit: hatvā bahuvidhāṃ senāṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ yuddhadurmadaḥ kathaṃ cit saṃkaṭān mukto mattadviradavikramaḥ
english: Having slain the manifold army of the Pāṇḍavas, that warrior fierce in battle, with the prowess of a rutting elephant, freed himself only with difficulty from the peril.

sanskrit: dravamāṇaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā palāyanakṛtakṣaṇam duryodhanaṃ samāsādya droṇaputro 'bravīd idam
english: Seeing the army in flight, with no thought but to flee, the son of Droṇa came up to Duryodhana and spoke these words.

sanskrit: kim iyaṃ dravate senā trastarūpeva bhārata dravamāṇāṃ ca rājendra nāvasthāpayase raṇe
english: "Why does this army flee as though in terror, O Bhārata? And why, O king of kings, do you not halt it in the battle as it flees?

sanskrit: tvaṃ cāpi na yathāpūrvaṃ prakṛtistho narādhipa karṇaprabhṛtayaś ceme nāvatiṣṭhanti pārthivāḥ
english: You too, O ruler of men, are not as you were before, settled in your nature; and these kings, Karṇa and the rest, do not hold their ground.

sanskrit: anyeṣv api ca yuddheṣu naiva senādravat tadā kaccit kṣemaṃ mahābāho tava sainyasya bhārata
english: In other battles too the army never fled like this then. Is all well, O mighty-armed one, with this host of yours, O Bhārata?

sanskrit: kasminn idaṃ hate rājan rathasiṃhe balaṃ tava etām avasthāṃ saṃprāptaṃ tan mamācakṣva kaurava
english: At the slaying of what lion among chariot-warriors, O king, has this army of yours come to such a plight? Tell me that, O Kaurava."

sanskrit: tat tu duryodhanaḥ śrutvā droṇaputrasya bhāṣitam ghoram apriyam ākhyātuṃ nāśakat pārthivarṣabhaḥ
english: But Duryodhana, hearing this speech of Droṇa's son, that bull among kings, could not bring himself to tell the dread and grievous tidings.

sanskrit: bhinnā naur iva te putro nimagnaḥ śokasāgare bāṣpeṇa pihito dṛṣṭvā droṇaputraṃ rathe sthitam
english: Your son, like a shattered boat, was sunk in the sea of grief, his sight veiled with tears as he gazed upon the son of Droṇa standing in his chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ śāradvataṃ rājā savrīḍam idam abravīt śaṃseha sarvaṃ bhadraṃ te yathā sainyam idaṃ drutam
english: Then the king said this to the son of Śaradvat, in shame, "Tell here everything—blessings upon you—how it is that this army has fled."

sanskrit: atha śāradvato rājann ārtiṃ gacchan punaḥ punaḥ śaśaṃsa droṇaputrāya yathā droṇo nipātitaḥ
english: Then the son of Śaradvat, O king, sinking again and again into anguish, recounted to the son of Droṇa how Droṇa had been struck down.

sanskrit: kṛpa uvāca vayaṃ droṇaṃ puraskṛtya pṛthivyāṃ pravaraṃ ratham prāvartayāma saṃgrāmaṃ pāñcālair eva kevalaiḥ
english: Kṛpa said: Setting Droṇa before us, the foremost chariot-warrior upon earth, we joined battle with the Pāñcālas alone.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravṛtte saṃgrāme vimiśrāḥ kurusomakāḥ anyonyam abhigarjantaḥ śastrair dehān apātayan
english: Then, when the battle was joined, the Kurus and Somakas, mingling together and roaring at one another, brought down each other's bodies with their weapons.

sanskrit: tato droṇo brāhmam astraṃ vikurvāṇo nararṣabhaḥ ahanac chātravān bhallaiḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then Droṇa, that bull among men, wielding the Brahmā weapon, slew his foes with broad-headed shafts by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāḥ kekayā matsyāḥ pāñcālāś ca viśeṣataḥ saṃkhye droṇarathaṃ prāpya vyanaśan kālacoditāḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas, the Kekayas, the Matsyas, and the Pāñcālas above all, coming up against Droṇa's chariot in battle, perished, driven on by fate.

sanskrit: sahasraṃ rathasiṃhānāṃ dvisāhasraṃ ca dantinām droṇo brahmāstranirdagdhaṃ preṣayām āsa mṛtyave
english: A thousand lions among chariot-warriors and two thousand elephants Droṇa, having scorched them with the Brahmā weapon, dispatched to death.

sanskrit: ākarṇapalitaḥ śyāmo vayasāśītipañcakaḥ raṇe paryacarad droṇo vṛddhaḥ ṣoḍaśavarṣavat
english: Gray-haired to the ears, dark of hue, eighty-five years of age, Droṇa, old as he was, ranged the battle like one of sixteen years.

sanskrit: kliśyamāneṣu sainyeṣu vadhyamāneṣu rājasu amarṣavaśam āpannāḥ pāñcālā vimukhābhavan
english: As the armies were sorely afflicted and the kings were being slain, the Pāñcālas, given over to wrath, turned their faces from the fight.

sanskrit: teṣu kiṃ cit prabhagneṣu vimukheṣu sapatnajit divyam astraṃ vikurvāṇo babhūvārka ivoditaḥ
english: When they were somewhat broken and had turned away, the vanquisher of his rivals, wielding a celestial weapon, became like the risen sun.

sanskrit: sa madhyaṃ prāpya pāṇḍūnāṃ śararaśmiḥ pratāpavān madhyaṃgata ivādityo duṣprekṣyas te pitābhavat
english: Reaching the midst of the Pāṇḍavas, that majestic one, his arrows for rays, became hard to look upon, like the sun arrived at its zenith—your father did.

sanskrit: te dahyamānā droṇena sūryeṇeva virājatā dagdhavīryā nirutsāhā babhūvur gatacetasaḥ
english: Burned by Droṇa, who blazed like the sun, their valor scorched away, they grew dispirited and lost their senses.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā pīḍitān bāṇair droṇena madhusūdanaḥ jayaiṣī pāṇḍuputrāṇām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing them tormented by Droṇa's arrows, the Slayer of Madhu, desiring the victory of the sons of Pāṇḍu, spoke these words.

sanskrit: naiṣa jātu paraiḥ śakyo jetuṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ api vṛtrahaṇā saṃkhye rathayūthapayūthapaḥ
english: "This foremost of weapon-bearers can never be vanquished in battle by his foes, not even by the slayer of Vṛtra—he, the chief of chariot-troop leaders."

sanskrit: te yūyaṃ dharmam utsṛjya jayaṃ rakṣata pāṇḍavāḥ yathā vaḥ saṃyuge sarvān na hanyād rukmavāhanaḥ
english: "Therefore do you, O Pāṇḍavas, set righteousness aside and guard the victory, so that he of the golden car may not slay you all in the battle."

sanskrit: aśvatthāmni hate naiṣa yudhyed iti matir mama hataṃ taṃ saṃyuge kaś cid ākhyātv asmai mṛṣā naraḥ
english: "With Aśvatthāman slain, he would fight no more—such is my thought. Let some man falsely tell him that he has been slain in the battle."

sanskrit: etan nārocayad vākyaṃ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ arocayaṃs tu sarve 'nye kṛcchreṇa tu yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: This counsel found no favor with Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī; but all the others approved it, and Yudhiṣṭhira too, though with difficulty.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu savrīḍam abravīt pitaraṃ tava aśvatthāmā hata iti tac cābudhyata te pitā
english: Then Bhīmasena, in shame, said to your father, "Aśvatthāman is slain!"—and your father came to know of this.

sanskrit: sa śaṅkamānas tan mithyā dharmarājam apṛcchata hataṃ vāpy ahataṃ vājau tvāṃ pitā putravatsalaḥ
english: Suspecting that this was false, your father, fond of his son, asked the King of Righteousness whether he had been slain or not slain in the fight.

sanskrit: tadatathyabhaye magno jaye sakto yudhiṣṭhiraḥ aśvatthāmānam āhedaṃ hataḥ kuñjara ity uta bhīmena girivarṣmāṇaṃ mālavasyendravarmaṇaḥ
english: Sunk in the dread of speaking untruth, yet bent upon victory, Yudhiṣṭhira said this concerning Aśvatthāman—"the elephant"—that had been slain by Bhīma, the mountain-bodied beast of Indravarman of the Mālavas: "He is slain."
